title: La partera
goal: Talk to a midwife who has delivered half the street
culture: The parteras delivered most people over forty in this barrio, at home, without a doctor, and they are respected accordingly. She is not a folk curiosity and this is not a mission about quaintness — she did a hard job well for fifty years and she is the right person to ask about it.

beats.es: Siéntese, mi hijo. ¿Usted es el que anda preguntando por el barrio?
beats.objective: Ask how long she has been doing it
beats.en: Yes. How many years have you been a midwife?
ok: si cuantos anos tiene de partera
beats.good: ¿Cuántos años? asks the number and gets you the life. It is the same question you ask about a house, a job or a marriage here.

beats.es: Cincuenta y dos años, mi hijo. Desde los diecinueve.
beats.objective: Ask about the children of this street
beats.en: And they were all born here?
beats.good: Aquí nacieron — they were born here, in these rooms, on this street. Half the people you have met in this district came through her hands.

beats.es: Aquí mismo. En sus casas, en su cama.
beats.good: Ask it plainly. It is not a challenge and she will not take it as one — the hospital was far and there was petrol money to find.

beats.es: Sin doctor. Y nunca se me murió ninguno, gracias a Dios. Ninguno.
beats.say: Nunca se le murió ninguno. Qué grande.
beats.en: You never lost one. That’s something.
ok: nunca se le murio ninguno que grande
beats.good: Nunca se me murió from her, nunca se le murió from you — the same fact, and the little pronoun carries the whole weight of it. Qué grande is admiration, not size.
